repository_purpose: Real-time multi-agent observability stack that captures hook events, stores them durably, and streams them to a live dashboard.
findings: The key reusable primitive is the event pipeline (`hook script -> HTTP POST -> SQLite -> WebSocket`), not the Vue dashboard itself.
Session boundaries, event-type filtering, and top-level forwarding of fields like `tool_name`, `tool_use_id`, and `agent_id` give the parent enough structure to define a durable ingest contract.
The upstream repo already includes stop-hook guards against self-referential observability loops, which is relevant to the parent no-fake-green doctrine.

capability_rows.upstream_feature_name: hook event ingest with session-correlated telemetry
capability_rows.validation_method: Validate event emission, session start/end markers, correlation fields, durable ingest, and queryable swimlane views before observability claims are promoted.
capability_rows.blocker_or_dependency: Requires a running ingest sink (Bun/HTTP plus durable store) or an equivalent local sidecar; otherwise the lane must stay blocked or fixture-only.

trigger_logic: Emit events on prompt, tool, session, and subagent lifecycle boundaries.
Require ingest availability or an exact blocked state before claiming multi-agent observability.
actor_logic: Mesh verifier owns correlated ingest and promotion-time trace review.
Emitters stay decoupled from storage so the parent can swap local sinks without changing event semantics.
validation_summary: Require durable storage plus queryable session and event filters.
Require explicit stop/session-end evidence so runs do not look green only because traces ended silently.

overlaps: Hook-policy packet supplies the event taxonomy and fail-loud validators.
Reports and artifact-registry Notion docs explain how telemetry should feed run reports and scorecards.
blockers: Live ingest depends on a local or remote sink actually being configured; without that, only fixture or schema evidence is truthful.
